raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

GLM shared-indexer layers reuse another layer's top-k result and do not write their own indexer keys. HiSparse currently disables the existing shared-layer index-K elision policy, so it still allocates logical-length index-K buffers for those layers. For a 78-layer GLM layout with 21 full indexers, this allocates 57 unused buffers.

## Modifications

- Add opt-in `SGLANG_ENABLE_HISPARSE_INDEX_K_ELISION=1` (default off).
- Restrict it to CUDA `glm_moe_dsa` target workers in PD decode, with PP/attention CP/DCP all 1, no external cache linker, and a valid full/shared indexer layout beginning with a full indexer. Draft workers keep their own storage. Unsupported configurations retain the old allocation policy.
- Apply the same eligibility policy to actual index-K allocation and token-pool memory budgeting. Leave target attention KV and independent draft KV/index-K intact.
- Preserve layer-aligned zero-row placeholders and raw getter behavior, including transfer-counter advancement. Reject attempts to run indexer read/write kernels on shared layers; do not confuse non-owned CP layers with shared layers.
- Log the active indexer-layer count and allocated index-K bytes.

Enable the flag on the decode engine before launch. It is independent of the HiSparse swap-in prefetch flag. An explicit `--max-total-tokens` cap still limits the resulting logical capacity; elision does not remove that cap or change the model context length.

## Accuracy Tests

CPU regressions: **193 passed, 161 subtests passed, 4 GPU tests skipped** across:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=999 python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hisparse_index_elision.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_dsa_pool_host_unit.py \
  test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_disaggregation_wire.py \
  test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_pool_configurator.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_npu_index_k_elision.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_kv_cache_configurator_npu_indexer.py
```

The GPU file was also run separately on an H100: **5 passed, 4 subtests passed**, including both newly added GPU regressions:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_dsa_pool_host_unit.py
```

Coverage includes exact byte accounting against actual allocated CPU tensors at ratios 16/20/32, preserved draft storage, PD layer IDs, NPU exclusion, raw getter placeholders, and CUDA L2 indexer/KV round trips with a packed draft and a PP stage that begins on a shared layer. No full-model accuracy results are claimed for this upstream port.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

This change reduces allocated index-K storage; it does not change top-k computation. For the tested GLM layout, active target index-K buffers drop from 78 to 21, reducing that component's storage by 57/78 (about 73%). This is not a 73% reduction in total GPU memory. No inference-throughput claim.

## Validation scope

Ported and tested independently on upstream `045e0e2e2d7d976c9351c949ed3d41527ac2871f`. The other HiSparse changes in this series are not included in this branch. Tests below exercise production Python code with small pools and mocked transport/control-plane dependencies; they are not a full distributed model benchmark.

## Checklist

- [x] Run isort and the repository-pinned Ruff formatting/lint checks on changed Python files.
- [x] Add targeted regression tests.
- [x] Run `git diff --check`.
- [ ] Full distributed model accuracy/performance validation on this upstream revision.
